data.body:
Implemented on branch fix/34cd-autodeploy-drain (commit db241b80ab), committed locally, NOT pushed.

## Root cause is sharper than "no drain at all"

The bot ALREADY drains on shutdown, but only half of it. `app.py`'s lifespan does
`await asyncio.wait_for(queue.join(), timeout=shutdown_drain_seconds())` with a 1200s budget,
and compose gives it `stop_grace_period: 1320s` — both far exceed the ~10 min review. So a
webhook-queued review IS protected today.

The backfill reconciler is NOT. `reconcile_once` awaits `review_and_vote` INLINE, outside the
queue, so `queue.join()` returns immediately and the reconcile_loop task is cancelled within
SHUTDOWN_CANCEL_SECONDS (10s). And the reconciler is precisely the path that RETRIES a killed
review. That is the live-lock mechanism: deploy kills the review, reconciler retries, next
deploy kills the retry — the self-heal path is the unprotected one.

Verified by code reading on origin/main (d4095763e3), not inferred.

## Option chosen: (b) DEFER

- (a) DRAIN rejected: sleeping until idle holds the deploy `flock` for up to the bound, blocking
  the obs/certbot re-materializers and every other tick for ~10+ min.
- (c) COALESCE rejected as insufficient alone: a debounce reduces seven deploys to fewer but a
  single deploy still kills a review, so it cannot satisfy AC1. It also delays idle-bot deploys
  for no safety gain.
- (b) DEFER chosen: the unit is an idempotent oneshot timer, so "come back in ~2 min" is free and
  holds no lock. It also COALESCES for free — TARGET is recomputed every tick, so a run of
  deferred ticks collapses into ONE deploy at the newest tip. (b) therefore subsumes (c)'s
  benefit without (c)'s cost, so (c) was not implemented.

Deviation from the plan worth flagging: the plan grouped (b) with "needs no new bot surface", but
deferring requires a busy signal. Implemented as the minimum: an `in_flight` field added to the
EXISTING `/health` route (no new endpoint, no new URL to configure, `status` unchanged). autodeploy
already polls HEALTH_URL for its readiness gate.

Counter is bracketed around `review_and_vote`, which is the single funnel for BOTH the worker and
the reconciler — so the signal sees the unprotected path, which is the whole point.

## Bound (AC2): DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX=1800s, keyed to the EPISODE not the SHA

Rationale: the bot wraps every review in `asyncio.wait_for(..., REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)` on both
paths (default 1200s), so no single review can outlive that and in_flight necessarily reaches 0
within it. 1800s is 1.5x that ceiling and ~3x the measured ~10 min review, so the bound is only
reachable by a CHRONICALLY busy bot, never by one ordinary review. A test reads
DEFAULT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and asserts bound >= it, keeping the two in lockstep.

Subtlety caught while implementing: keying the bound to the target SHA the way BACKOFF_FILE does
would DEFEAT the bound — during a burst TARGET advances almost every tick, so the timer would
reset before it could expire and a permanently-busy bot would defer forever. The bound is keyed
to the deferral EPISODE, cleared on deploy / idle / up-to-date. Two tests cover this (bound
survives a changing SHA; a stale episode cannot kill a later review's first tick).

## AC4 observability — the blind spot is now alarmed

Two new countable tokens, deliberately NOT folded into AUTODEPLOY_ERROR (a routine deferral must
not page):
- AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED -> rebar/host:deploy_deferrals (informational)
- AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT -> rebar/host:review_interrupts + a NEW paging CloudWatch alarm
  `rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts` (monitoring_autodeploy.tf). Emitted when the bound is spent
  (`bound-exceeded`) OR when the in_flight signal is unreadable (`signal-unavailable`).

The `signal-unavailable` case matters: the drain fails OPEN on an unreadable signal (a bot that
cannot answer /health is likely broken, and deploying is how it gets fixed — blocking deploys on
an unparseable field would invent a new way to freeze the gate), but a silently broken probe would
restore the original blindness, so it is counted. A /health payload MISSING in_flight counts as
unknown, never as idle.

## Tests (bash tested via the existing stub-binary harness)

Precedent reused: tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_health_gate.py stubs git/docker/curl/flock onto
PATH and runs the REAL script via subprocess. Extended it by making the target SHA and the /health
body FILE-backed, so a test can change them between ticks — that is what makes a burst testable.

tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py (13 tests) + tests/unit/test_review_bot_in_flight.py
(8 tests). AC5 burst test: six ticks arrive with the tip advancing each time while one review runs
— asserts ZERO recreations across the whole burst, then exactly ONE compose-build at the NEWEST
tip.

NOT vacuous: reverted autodeploy.sh to HEAD and re-ran — 10 of 13 failed (the 3 that passed assert
already-correct behaviour: idle deploys, unreachable bot still deployable). Genuine RED.

## Gates (exit codes, from the worktree venv, clean tree)

make lint 0 · make typecheck 0 · check_config_reads.py 0 · gen_env_registry.py --check 0
pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6: 9605 passed, 42 skipped, 1 failed.

The 1 failure is PRE-EXISTING and unrelated: test_comment_hygiene_guard::test_the_real_tree_is_clean
flags run-id 30836378745 in tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py and
tests/external/test_provider_matrix_live.py. Reproduced identically on base d4095763e3 in a clean
temp worktree (same 3 findings), and neither file is touched by this change.

voter.py 733 LOC, under the 800 cap.
